items.description: Costa Rica's national stadium in La Sabana, designed as a major modern sports venue. It is the country's top football ground and a visible city landmark.
A bridge over the Tempisque River that improved access to the Nicoya Peninsula. It is one of the most useful transport links in Guanacaste.
An interactive children's museum in a former prison building in San Jose. It mixes education, play, and historic architecture in one place.
The Central Post Office of Costa Rica, a historic building in downtown San Jose. Its palace-like design makes it one of the city's most recognizable heritage sites.
Costa Rica's main art museum, located in the former La Sabana airport terminal. It holds an important national collection and a strong architectural presence.
An iconic bandstand in Morazan Park, better known as the Temple of Music. It is a small but important symbol of downtown San Jose.
A cultural complex in a former liquor factory in San Jose. Today it houses theaters, galleries, and public cultural spaces.
The famous metal church of Grecia, made from prefabricated steel plates. Its red neo-Gothic form makes it one of the country's best-known architectural curiosities.
The home stadium of Deportivo Saprissa in Tibas. Fans know it as La Cueva, one of the most intense football venues in Costa Rica.
A colonial church in Orosi and one of the oldest still-used churches in Costa Rica. It is a key landmark in the Orosi Valley's historic landscape.
A modern event venue in Alajuela used for concerts, fairs, and motorsport. It is one of the country's biggest contemporary entertainment spaces.
A distinctive stone church in the hills of Heredia. Its strong local profile makes it a familiar landmark for the surrounding canton.
